name: Sunk Cost Fallacy
shortDef: Continuing something because of what's already been spent, not what's ahead.
definition: Letting money, time or effort that is already spent and can't be recovered drive a decision about the future, instead of weighing only the costs and benefits still to come.
howToSpot: Is the main reason to continue what has already been spent?
If you were starting fresh today, would you still choose this?
Does continuing recover the past investment, or is it gone either way?
classicExample: This movie is awful, but we paid $18 a ticket, so we're staying until the end.
legitimateVersion: Continuing is reasonable when the remaining benefits outweigh the remaining costs, like finishing a nearly done renovation because the last step adds more value than it costs.

contrast.fal_appeal_to_tradition: Sunk cost keeps going because of what has been invested; appeal to tradition keeps going because it has always been done that way.
contrast.fal_appeal_to_consequences: Sunk cost looks back at what was spent; appeal to consequences judges a claim by whether its outcome would be pleasant.
